subject.title: [Bug]: `openclaw models auth login` on node host writes OAuth token locally instead of syncing to gateway

question: Should remote node-host `openclaw models auth login` fail closed before provider auth starts, or should OpenClaw design gateway-side credential forwarding for this flow?
rationale: Both directions change a sensitive provider credential boundary, and automation should not choose whether node hosts may acquire and transfer gateway-owned OAuth material without maintainer intent.

options.title: Fail closed before auth starts
options.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable gateway-host instruction and preserve local loopback/tunnel setups with shared loopback semantics.

options.title: Forward credentials to the gateway
options.body: Design an authenticated gateway RPC or setup flow that moves provider auth material to the gateway store without consuming tokens locally first.

options.title: Warn but keep permissive
options.body: Warn node-host users that auth will only affect the local node, accepting the current wrong-host credential risk for compatibility.

recommendation.title: Fail closed before auth starts
recommendation.body: Block non-loopback remote node-host auth login with an actionable gateway-host instruction and preserve local loopback/tunnel setups with shared loopback semantics.

likelyOwner.reason: Vincent already authored and verified the maintainer repair direction for this exact remote-node auth guard.
